decisions.quote:
The purpose of the present study was to attempt to
replicate the Vernon et al. (in press) finding that individual differences in affiliative and self-enhancing
humor were largely attributable to additive genetic
and nonshared environmental factors, whereas individual differences in aggressive and self-defeating
humor were largely attributable to shared and nonshared environmental factors.
In contrast to Vernon et al. (in press), we found
here that all four styles of humor were best fit by an
additive genetic and nonshared environmental model,
with the styles showing heritabilities ranging from .34
to .49.
decisions.reason: This paper is a completed empirical replication using a new UK sample of 1,073 MZ and 895 same-sex DZ adult twin pairs to re-test Vernon, Martin, Schermer, and Mackie (in press / 2008, Personality and Individual Differences). The outcome is 'mixed' because all four humor styles were best fit by an additive genetic and nonshared environmental (AE) model, which confirmed the original finding for the two positive humor styles (affiliative and self-enhancing) but contrasted with the original finding of shared and nonshared environmental (CE) influences for the two negative humor styles (aggressive and self-defeating), as the authors explicitly state both at the start and in the conclusion of the Discussion.
